column4: Alternative Fuels Program for Transportation and Other Purposes (AFPTOP)
column6:
The AFTOP is designed to encourage the diversification of fuel sources and energy technologies across both transport and non-transport sectors. The primary objective of the program is to enhance energy security and promote environmental protection.

Energy Security
AFTOP aims to reduce reliance on conventional fossil fuels by promoting alternative fuels. This strategy involves exploring sustainable and cleaner energy options, which enhances energy security by:
•Decreasing dependence on a single fuel type;
•Mitigating risks associated with fuel price fluctuations; and
•Reducing vulnerability to supply disruptions.

Environmental Protection
AFTOP also places a significant emphasis on environmental protection. The program recognizes that conventional fossil fuels contribute to air pollution and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, which have detrimental effects on both human health and the environment. By encouraging the use of alternative fuels such as hydrogen, electricity, sustainable aviation fuel, and other emerging technologies, AFTOP aims to:
•Reduce emissions;
•Promote cleaner air quality; and
•Mitigate the impacts of climate change.

Implementation and Goals
AFTOP seeks to create an enabling environment for the mainstream adoption of alternative fuels in both transport and non-transport sectors through various initiatives, including:
•Policy measures;
•Research initiatives;
•Demonstration projects; and
•Promotional activities.

By supporting the transition towards cleaner and more sustainable energy options, AFTOP aligns with broader national goals of energy diversification, energy security, and environmental sustainability.

column4: Ilocos Norte-Ilocos Sur-Abra Irrigation Project (Formerly Ilocos Norte Irrigation Project, Stage 2)
column6:
The INISAIP, which encompasses the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, and Abra, is designed as a multipurpose development project that involves the following components:

 a. Construction of an earth and rockfill dam with a height of 126.41 meters (m), length of 480.00 m, and crest width of 10.00 m across Palsiguan River, within the municipality of Lagayan in the Province of Abra. A 0.68-kilometer (km) headrace tunnel and an 8.12-km tailrace tunnel will convey the water from an intake structure to be located at the mid-portion of the reservoir area;
 b. Construction of the Nueva Era afterbay dam, which shall serve as the re-regulating structure in the delivery of irrigation water to approximately 4,982 ha of service area within the Ilocos Norte Irrigation Project (INIP)-1, through the 38.40 km Link Canal No. 1; and
 c. Construction of Link Canals No. 2 and 3, with a total length of 24.87 km that will provide irrigation water to the 9,690 ha of service area within INIP-2, covering the following NIS: (i) Batac-Paoay River Irrigation System (RIS); (ii) Badoc-Sinait RIS; (iii) Pinili RIS; (iv) Madupayas RIS; and (v) Nueva Era-left bank.

The project intends to irrigate approximately 14,672 ha. (during the wet season) and 13, 256 (during the dry season) of agricultural lands, with the Palsiguan River as the main source of irrigation water and will be conveyed to different sub-areas through a network of link canals.

Additionally, the project will include provisions for the implementation of power components, i.e., HEPPs and solar power farm, which will be implemented through Public-Private Partnership (PPP).

Secondly, the project seeks to raise public awareness about the benefits of using biofuels. Biofuels are renewable energy sources derived from organic materials, such as plant crops or waste products. By educating the public about the advantages of biofuels, such as reduced greenhouse gas emissions and support for local agriculture, the project aims to increase acceptance and adoption of these eco-friendly fuel options.

Overall, the project's objectives align with the broader goals of achieving sustainable energy practices, reducing environmental challenges, and ensuring a secure and diversified energy supply. By promoting alternative fuels and enhancing public awareness, the project contributes to a more sustainable and environment friendly energy future.

column4: National Broadband Program
column5: Department of Information and Communications Technology
column6:
The NBP is one of the major flagship programs of the DICT to close the digital divide and elevate Filipinos’ living standards by deploying broadband capacity across the nation, especially in areas that are remote, inaccessible, and considered unprofitable by the private sector. 

To mobilize and engage both the public and private sectors, the NBP intends to identify and develop approaches in engaging both aforementioned sectors’ stakeholders to collaborate and contribute towards the realization of the National Broadband Plan’s objectives of providing fast, reliable, and affordable broadband internet access. 

The NBP has three (3) strategies through which the outcomes can be supported. These are:

Institute Policy and Regulatory Reforms – existing ICT policy and regulatory framework will be reviewed, and amended to become more responsive to the current needs of the sector. 
Provide Government Investment in Broadband Infostructure – the government intends to establish the Infostructure needed to address the bottlenecks in backbone and backhaul segments and augment the bandwidth requirements of the country. This will also provide the core and aggregation network for national government agencies (NGAs), local government units (LGUs), state universities and colleges (SUCs), rural health units (RHUs), public schools, and public hospitals, among others. This will also help leverage the existing government assets and initiatives 
Support on the Stimulation of Broadband Demand – to help sustain the momentum of providing pervasive infostructure, the government will establish “pull” measures to stimulate demand through (i) local content development and promotion, (ii) conduct of capacity building and information outreach programs, such as Government Network (GovNet), FPIAP, and Tech4ED to lower implementation costs and reach Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDA). and (iii) introduction of incentives to broadband users.

Components of the NBP:

National Fiber Backbone (NFB)
Government Network (GovNet) 

Beneficiaries:

All components of the NBP directly benefit government agencies and other public institutions, including National Government Agencies (NGAs); LGUs; Public Hospitals, Health Centers, and Rural Health Units (RHUs); State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) technology institutions; Public Parks, Plazas, Libraries, and Barangay Reading Centers; Public Primary and Secondary Schools; Public Airports and Seaports; Public Transport Terminals; and other line agencies and stakeholders.

column4: Free Wi-Fi for all - Free Public Internet Access Program
column5: Department of Information and Communications Technology
column6:
The Department of Information and Communications Technology’s Free Public Internet Access Program (FPIAP) aims to accelerate the Philippine government’s efforts in enhancing internet accessibility for Filipinos so that economic, social, and educational opportunities will be bolstered, and the growing digital divide can be bridged.

FPIAP ultimately aims to empower the Filipino people digitally by tapping existing technology and ensuring that the benefits to be derived from these advancements are available to everyone. Internet access, after all, should not be a privilege enjoyed by few but a right enjoyed by all.

Connectivity services under the Program had been envisioned to be utilized for educational (e.g., enrollment in online courses, access to reference materials and productivity tools), socio-economic (e.g., web-based work, access to government services), and communication (e.g., email, social media, messaging platforms via internet purposes.

The Program’s vision of Internet for all is a shared one, however. As such, further expansion of ICT services through public-private participation is an integral component of Program implementation. Further, the Program’s goal to provide Internet access in all public places is aligned with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028 strategy of modernizing and expanding digital infrastructure through effective ICT governance and policy regulation, public and private investments, and strategic collaborations, as the Program, along with the other DICT flagship programs, is poised to facilitate the expansion of the digital infrastructure up to the Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs), and address the disparity in access and cost of digital services.

column4: Philippine General Hospital Diliman (UP SYSTEM)
column6:
The Philippine General Hospital was created by the Philippine Commission Act of 1608 in 1907. Its mandate was to serve the poor Filipino. It opened its doors to the public on 01 September 1910 under the Department of Interiors with Dr. Victor Heiser as the first director. In 1939, President Manuel L. Quezon placed the control of the hospital under the Dean of the College of Medicine. Immediately after the war, 01 July 1945, the Department of Public Health took control of it and its rebuilding, and in 1947 President Manuel A. Roxas transferred it back to the University of the Philippines System, designating PGH as its teaching hospital. The separation of the position of the Dean of the College Medicine and Director of the Hospital was effected in 1954 with an Executive Order of President Ramon Magsaysay. 

The UP Manila Health Sciences Center was established with Republic Act No. 3163 in 1967.
 
On 21 December 1983, Executive Order No. 11 asserted the mandate of PGH as primarily teaching and service its secondary function.
 
In 2001, Regent Victor Reyes opined that the growing challenges of health care to the public made it necessary to redefine the primary function of PGH. In its 1153rd meeting held on 30 August 2001, the Board of Regents approved the amendment of the policy of function of PGH: 

"The primary function of the Philippine General Hospital is the care of the sick and injured of the community. As the largest government facility and referral center, it must endeavor to remain abreast of medical care and hospital operations. 

A concomitant responsibility of the Philippine General Hospital is the expansion of knowledge through educational endeavor and scientific research. As the clinical venue of the College of Medicine and other academic units, it must function as an integral part of the university in undergraduate and graduate education." 

This fell in place with the expansion of the services of the hospital, having built a 400-bed private hospital and a Faculty Medical Arts Building (FMAB), it was meeting head on the challenges of serving almost 600,000 patients a year. Currently, PGH stands on a 10-hectare site within UP Manila, employing more than 4,000 employees to run its services and needing an internal operating budget of almost Php 4 billion to make it function efficiently and effectively. 

With the Universal Healthcare Program supported by PhilHealth, partial funding for the hospital operations has been more consistent and sufficient. This, coupled with the share of PGH in the funds generated from Sin Tax, the Department of Health sub-allotments and other funding coming from various offices in government enabled the hospital to deliver the most advanced health services with no out-of- pocket expense from the patient. 

With improvement of health care delivery, more patients are seeking the services of PGH. In 2016, the number of patients rose by 35,000 from the averages of the past ten years: 50 percent of patients were noted to come from the NCR, 30 percent from the Calabarzon and the remaining 20 percent from the rest of the country, including the ARMM and Bontoc Province. It is predicted that as more advanced equipment and procedures/services are installed in PGH, many more patients will be flocking in. Hence, there is a real need to establish another facility to further expand the services and expertise provided by PGH.

column6:
The Infostructure Management Bureau (IMB) oversees the ICT Systems and Infrastructure Management and Services program, which handles the operation and maintenance of the government's core ICT infostructure, applications, networks, and related services. This overarching initiative is composed of four critical components:
Components and Key Activities
A. Operation and Maintenance of Government Network (GovNet) - (CIIMD) The Core ICT Infrastructure Management Division (CIIMD) manages and administers the government’s core network infrastructure, including the Free Wi-Fi for All and the National Broadband Network. Key activities include:
•	Maintenance of fiber optic networks for reliable connectivity.
•	Internet bandwidth subscriptions to support government operations.
•	Leasing of IP transport services for secure data transmission.
•	Management of a network system for performance oversight.
•	Upgrading existing infrastructure to meet increasing operational demands.
B. Operations and Maintenance of Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRMD) The Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Division (DRRMD) serves as the Department's main emergency operations center for telecommunications. It is designated as the Lead Agency of the Emergency Telecommunications Cluster within the NDRRMC to coordinate activities and disseminate vital information for disaster risk reduction and management. Key activities include:
•	Developing emergency response protocols leveraging telecommunications.
•	Implementing redundancy and backup systems.
•	Enhancing security measures for data protection.
•	Ensuring interoperability among agency communication systems.
•	Conducting training and simulations for crisis preparedness.
C. Operation and Maintenance of Government Online Services (GOSD) The Government Online Services Division (GOSD) operates and maintains essential government online services, including frontline, sectoral, and whole-of-government applications. Core services provided are:
•	Government Web Hosting Services (GWHS): Providing centralized web hosting for government entities.
•	Government Wide Email System (GovMail): Offering official user addresses to government agencies to enhance communication accountability.
•	.gov.ph Domain Registration/GovDNS Hosting: Registering and uniquely identifying Philippine government entities on the Internet.

D. Operations and Maintenance of the Government Data Centers (DCMD) The objective is to ensure that all government data centers are operated and maintained to fullest efficiency within a secured environment. This enables 24/7 service delivery in hosting, housing, and providing ICT services to government stakeholders. Key objectives are:
•	Provision of data center facilities that house critical ICT infrastructure.
•	Provision of central monitoring facilities for all related ICT services.
•	Ensuring the resiliency of the housed ICT infrastructure.
•	Maintaining 24/7 availability with an increased efficiency rating of 99.8%.
Beneficiaries
The program serves various government stakeholders, including:
•	National Government Agencies (NGAs)
•	Government-Owned and Controlled Corporations (GOCCs)
•	Government Financial Institutions (GFIs)
•	Local Government Units (LGUs)
•	State Universities and Colleges (SUCs)
•	Government Hospitals

column4: Strengthening the Safety and Security of the Radioactive Waste Management Infrastructure in the Philippines
column6:
The recent enactment of the Philippine Nuclear Energy Safety Act, also known as the PhilAtom Law, highlights the country's commitment to integrating nuclear energy into its national energy mix. According to the Philippine Energy Plan 2023–2050, nuclear energy is expected to contribute 1.2 GW of electricity by 2032, with a projected increase to 4.8 GW by 2050.

With the introduction of nuclear energy, new streams of radioactive waste will inevitably be generated—waste types for which the country currently has no prior experience in managing. This underscores the urgent need for a more robust radioactive waste management infrastructure, capable of handling large volumes and a broad spectrum of radionuclides produced during the operation and maintenance of nuclear power plants.

At present, the Radioactive Waste Management Facility (RWMF), operated by the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI), functions solely as a service provider under the Radiation Protection Services Section (RPSS). It manages only radioactive waste from non-power applications. The facility lacks full-time personnel dedicated to its operations and does not have a clearly defined funding allocation. These limitations—insufficient human and financial resources, coupled with inadequate infrastructure—restrict its operational capacity and render it unfit to support the country’s nuclear energy program or address existing gaps in the national radioactive waste management framework.

Fortunately, the PhilAtom Law mandates the establishment of a Low and Intermediate Level Radioactive Waste Management Office/Center under the PNRI. This new entity will be responsible for the comprehensive planning and execution of predisposal and disposal activities for low- and intermediate-level radioactive waste and it is anticipated that by 2027, the current PNRI-RWMF will be restructured into the PNRI–Low and Intermediate Level Radioactive Waste Management Center (RWMC).

This project is proposed to address the critical gaps in the country’s radioactive waste management infrastructure in preparation for waste arising from future nuclear power plants. Its overall objective is to support the PNRI-RWMC and ensure that, by 2032, the country has the capacity and capability to manage low- and/or intermediate-level waste generated from nuclear and radiation facilities with safety, security, and sustainability. 

To do this, the project aims to:
1. Strengthen the workforce capacity on managing low- and intermediate-level radioactive waste.
2. Modernize the existing predisposal facility to ensure its compliance with radiological and non-radiological safety and security requirements and to be capable of conducting research & development activities.
3. Investigate current and emerging radioactive waste management trends for waste arising from current and advance nuclear reactor technologies
4. Conduct preliminary studies and develop the conceptual design for the National Low and Intermediate Level Waste Management Site.

The ultimate goal of radioactive waste management is to safely handle and dispose of waste in a manner that protects human health and the environment, without imposing undue burdens on future generations. Achieving this requires a robust radioactive waste management infrastructure with a competent organization dedicated to its implementation. The establishment of the PNRI-Radioactive Waste Management Center (RWMC) is in alignment with international standards and best practices, as well as the PNRI’s vision and mission to be a national center of excellence in nuclear science and technology and enhance the quality of life for every Filipino, by leveraging our technical expertise in support of the Philippines' nuclear energy program.

column4: Maridagao (Kadingilan) Irrigation Project
column6:
The proposed Project is to be implemented in the municipalities of Kalilangan, Pangantucan, Don Carlos, and Kadingilan in the province of Bukidnon. The proposed development scheme envisions the construction of a diversion dam that will harness the potential of Maridagao River and Kidangin River. The total functionality of the structure will be ensured through the provision of irrigation and drainage facilities for a potential service area of 6,555 hectares.  

The proposed Maridagao Dam is geographically located at 07°41'42.08" north latitude and 124°44'34.10" east longitude. The proposed dam site is about 750 m horizontal distance from the highway. It is situated across on a stable moderately narrow section of the Maridagao River where the active river channel is about 40.00 meters wide. The proposed Kidangin Dam is geographically located at 07°42'21.83" north latitude and 124°49'6.11" east longitude. The dam site is accessible by land through the Davao-Bukidnon Highway, about 193)kilometers drive northwest of Davao City airport and a 2.94 kilometer distance of dirt road. From there, it is accessible only by foot due to unmaintained sandy-clay farm to market road and foot trail. It is situated across a narrow section of the Kidangin River where the active river channel is about 15.00 meters wide. The project will construct 21.60 km main canals and 109.85 km lateral canals.

column4: Rehabilitation/ Reconstruction/ Improvement, Operation and Maintenance of Kennon Road
column5: Department of Public Works and Highways
column6:
The project involves the rehabilitation/reconstruction and improvement of Kennon Road to prevent the road slope disasters such as soil collapse, rock fall, road slip, landslide, and river erosion that frequently occur along this road.

Kennon Road is one of the major access roads leading to the Benguet Province. It provides the shortest route from Rosario to Baguio City with a total length of 33.7 km. It starts at the intersection with Manila North Road in the municipality of Rosario, La Union and ends at a roundabout connected with Marcos Highway and Governor Pack Road. About 98% of Kennon Road passes along the Bued River Valley with several river crossings. It intersects several water tributaries which may cause possible flash floods, siltation, and debris flows. It also crosses Pugo fault between the poblacion area of Rosario and Rosario junction.

Kennon Road is classified as a primary national road under the jurisdiction of three (3) District Engineering Offices namely: La Union 2nd, Benguet 1st, and Baguio City DEOs. It is composed of 12.495 km. asphalt pavement and 21.196 km. concrete pavement. There are also 12 steel bridges and 6 concrete bridges along Kennon Road. Most of the bridges were constructed in 1968 and have a load limit of 10 tons.

This project aims to:
• Provide fast, safe, comfortable, and reliable means of transportation from Rosario to Baguio City, thus providing ease to motorists travelling to Benguet Province
• Prevent road slope disasters that frequently occur along this road such as soil collapse, rock fall, road slip, landslide, and river erosion, by installing slope protection/stabilization works and appropriate engineering countermeasures at identified sections of the road
• Rehabilitate/reconstruct the existing bridges in bad condition to ensure its structural integrity and increase its load limit
• Establish an adequate system to operate and maintain the thoroughfare as a toll road.

column4: ESTABLISHMENT OF WASTE DISPOSAL AND RECYCLING FACILITIES AT MAIN CAMPUS
column6:
Catanduanes State University (CatSU) recognizes the increasing complexity of solid waste management challenges within its Main Campus and its surrounding communities. The campus generates a diverse waste stream, primarily consisting of plastic and glass, which presents environmental, operational, and compliance concerns if not systematically managed. To address this, the University is initiating the establishment of waste disposal and recycling facilities that will enhance material recovery, minimize landfill dependency, and strengthen its compliance with Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. This law obliges higher education institutions to integrate sustainable waste management systems both in operations and academic practices, while ensuring alignment with local government solid waste management initiatives.

The project is designed to incorporate engineered solutions and structured waste segregation, treatment, and recycling processes. By developing facilities that meet prescribed standards, the University ensures proper collection, sorting, and recovery of recyclable materials such as plastics and glass, while reducing residual waste volumes. This will not only reduce environmental risks but also provide a replicable model for other State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) and local government units (LGUs) in the province. Additionally, the integration of waste management principles into the University’s curricula and research activities will create opportunities for innovation in recycling technologies and resource utilization, supporting both academic and operational objectives.

Beyond compliance and campus-level improvements, the establishment of dedicated waste disposal and recycling facilities contributes to a broader systems approach in resource efficiency and environmental management. The project strengthens the local waste value chain by enhancing recovery rates and reducing the volume of waste directed to disposal sites. At the same time, it promotes institutional resilience by embedding sustainable practices in the University’s day-to-day operations. This positions CatSU as a strategic partner in advancing provincial-level waste management systems and complements national initiatives aimed at reducing the country’s ecological footprint.

By enabling efficient resource recovery, reducing landfill dependence, and integrating waste management into education and research, the project directly supports sectoral priorities on ecological integrity and a clean, healthy environment as identified in the Philippine Development Plan. More importantly, it provides a practical platform for producing graduates who are equipped with technical competencies and sustainability-oriented mindsets, ensuring that waste management is not merely a compliance activity but a catalyst for long-term environmental stewardship and socio-economic development.

column4: Construction of Integrated Materials Recovery Facility and Automated System for Waste Management and Energy Generation
column6:
Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) is a key component in any recycling program. This facility facilitates commingled materials and then uses a combination of equipment and manual labor to sort and densify materials for further recycling and recovery stages. Modern MRFs integrate automation systems to increase productivity and enhance recycling potential. It is significantly important to establish an MRF in order to ensure that all materials that cannot be further recycled have been removed. The process also helps in producing high quality recyclables so that creation of high-quality new products can be easily attained. With the help of an automated system, sorting with high-quality recyclable products, and even recovery of high-valued materials can be realized. In this infrastructure project, the team envisioned establishing a state-of-the-art materials recovery facility that promotes the recovery, recycling and value-adding materials production from wastes generated within the university. Not only that, it is also envisaged that self-sustaining energy source fitting for the CSU energy requirement can be supplied by the proposed energy production from waste materials of the materials recovery facility.


Sorting of solid wastes that promotes recycling and recovery of usable materials is one of the major activities to be adopted as far as the ecological and environmental safeguarding are concerned. Notwithstanding the intrinsic benefits to the environment, recycling and materials recovery enables the development of new usable products, technologies, and even it creates livelihoods and jobs. As commonly known by many, different types of wastes are generated from different point sources, such as large establishments, for example, schools and universities. Caraga State University is a growing institution, and together with the fast improvement of the research facilities within the university is the corresponding increase in the volume of the generated wastes. In particular, solid wastes and liquid (chemical) wastes are ubiquitous for several reasons, (1) chemical wastes generated from different chemical laboratories and R&D Centers, (2) solid wastes generated from various offices, (3) other e-waste from the junked electronic materials, among others. Importantly, these wastes are all toxic and need to be sorted, and possibly, can be recycled using the materials recovery facility. The construction of the MRF in the University will also attract researchers to conduct studies that will aim to develop new usable products and technologies. This will not only increase the research productivity of the University but will also result in discoveries, patents, and creation of livelihood.

column4: Improving Growth Corridors in Mindanao Road Sector Project, Phase II
column5: Department of Public Works and Highways
column6:
The road subsector is the most important transport subsector in the Philippines. The national road network comprises 29,630 kilometers (km), or 14% of the total road network, and includes the main trunk roads, national primary arterial roads, and national secondary roads. An efficient road transport subsector is crucial for the Philippines’ economic growth and poverty reduction.

Mindanao is the second largest island in the Philippines, with a population of more than 20 million people. Despite being rich in natural resources, Mindanao has the highest poverty incidence of the Philippines’ three island groups (Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao), with a rate of 36.2%. This is largely because of civil conflict and low economic growth. Despite significant development in recent years, a number of infrastructure targets in the government’s Mindanao 2000 plan were not achieved because of the lack of coherent plans, inadequate government financial resources, and underinvestment.

The increasing impact of climate change, particularly flooding, is having a negative effect on the road network. Mindanao’s road network is less developed than the national network. While 82% of the national roads in Luzon and 89% in Visayas are paved, only 70% of the national roads in Mindanao are paved. Thus, a large part of the road network in Mindanao remains in need of improvement.

The Government of the Republic of the Philippines proposed the Improving Growth Corridors in Mindanao Road Project Phase 2 (IGCMRP-Phase 2) for funding by the Asian Development Bank (ADB). The project includes the construction/rehabiliation/improvement of 219.77 kilometers (km) of national primary, secondary, and tertiary roads in Mindanao. This include paving earth roads, replacing damaged road sections, widening existing roads, adding surface overlays, and replacing and strengthening bridges. The project roads will be designed with features to strengthen resilience to climate change. Among the structural and non-structural features included are elevated pavement levels, enhanced slope protection, and improved maintenance of drainage structures. Road safety on these roads will be improved through road safety community awareness campaigns.

IGCMRP-Phase 2 comprises of six (6) Sub-projects with ten (10) Contract Packages with a total length of 219.77 km including the rehabilitation or replacement of 41 bridges.

column4: Construction of Elevated Walkways and Students Skylounges - Campus Flood Mitigation USTP CDO Campus), (Phase 1 and Phase 2)
column5: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines
column6: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines (USTP) is located in Brgy. Lapasan is a portion of the barangay that is naturally swampy. This existing condition stagnates surface water absorption and runs off resulting in pluvial floods, especially during torrential weather conditions. These recurring impediments have affected the campus and its end-users from vacating flooded areas in the past years - having a great number of students and personnel displaced and stranded for hours causes loss of learning hours, absenteeism, and even an outbreak of waterborne diseases. Although the campus has implemented flood mitigation efforts, the proposed Elevated Walkway provides an additional solution to this problem. This project acts as an effective structural countermeasure to allow users to safely move from building to building or from the university to Limketkai Gateway in the course of flooding. This also aids the rescuers to navigate through the campus in events of operation. It also fosters civilian safety due to the separation of pedestrians from vehicular traffic. Furthermore, this project encourages users to walk more. The benefits of walking, even short strolls, are numerous and often discussed. Promoting this through design provides an opportunity to increase individuals’ quality of education, work, health, and well-being. The design promotes further cooling on the campus with the additional shaded areas under its path. Moreover, this elevated walkway meanders through trees and canopies, allowing the users to experience the whole campus site from a fresh perspective.

column4: Bicol River Basin Flood Control Project - Phase I, Stage I
column5: Department of Public Works and Highways
column6:
The Bicol River Basin, a vital area for agriculture, forestry, and fisheries, is highly prone to flooding due to its exposure to typhoons and heavy rainfall. To address this, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) through the Unified Project Management Office–Flood Control Management Cluster (UPMO-FCMC) implemented the Updating of the Master Plan and Feasibility Study of Flood Control for Bicol and Pampanga River Basins – Package 1 to mitigate disaster risks through structural and non-structural measures.

Phase I, identified as a priority project, consists of four stages aimed at managing storm-related disasters aggravated by climate change. Stage I involves constructing setback road dikes along the Bicol River, Cut-off Channel, and Libmanan River, covering the municipalities of Canaman, Gainza, Libmanan, Magarao, Milaor, Minalabac, Pamplona, and San Fernando in Camarines Sur. These works are designed to reduce flooding by increasing the river’s capacity and accelerating floodwater discharge into San Miguel Bay, providing a long-term solution to the region’s recurring floods.

column6:
The construction of a 3C Air Traffic Control (ATC) Tower is a critical first-phase aviation infrastructure project that will allow APECO to manage safe and efficient domestic flight operations. Designed according to ICAO standards for Class 3C aerodromes, the tower will house the primary air navigation and surveillance systems, radio communication equipment, and meteorological monitoring instruments essential for regional flight coordination. It will serve as the operational center for air traffic controllers who will oversee all aircraft movements on the runway, taxiways, and within APECO’s airspace. The tower will also be built with climate-resilient architecture to withstand typhoons and seismic activity typical of the eastern seaboard.

Beyond operational control, the 3C ATC Tower lays the foundation for APECO’s aviation growth strategy. As the ecozone anticipates increased tourism, cargo movement, and business jet traffic, the tower ensures compliance with international safety protocols while enhancing confidence among airline operators. The tower’s strategic placement within the airport complex will also support future expansions, including its potential integration into a 4C facility, allowing it to scale with the zone’s broader transportation and economic development goals.

column4: Renovation of the FPRDI Xylarium Facility
column5: Forest Products Research and Development Institute
column6:
The DOST Forest Products Research and Development Institute (DOST-FPRDI) houses a unique Xylarium Facility, which contains an extensive collection of wood samples from Philippine trees, representing about 98% of the country's tree species. The facility stores approximately 10,983 samples, including around 2,282 species from 197 plant families, alongside nearly 10,000 foreign wood samples. This collection was initiated by Maj. George P. Ahern in the early 1900s but suffered significant losses during World War II. Today, DOST-FPRDI is crucial for wood identification services, assisting various sectors including the wood-based industry and government agencies in combating illegal logging.
To preserve this invaluable collection, DOST-FPRDI is implementing a project that includes installing a vault for secure storage, upgrading fire suppression systems, and enhancing electrical and drainage systems. The digitization of the wood library is also underway, allowing easier access to information about each sample via QR codes. This initiative not only protects historical specimens but also supports sustainable practices by ensuring compliance with regulations concerning wood sourcing. The efforts aim to maintain the integrity of the collection as many represented species are now endangered or extinct in the wild.

column4: Philippine Geothermal Resource Derisking Facility
column6:
The Philippine Geothermal Resource Development Facility (PGRDF) is a government-backed initiative designed to accelerate the development of the Philippines’ geothermal energy sector. To achieve this, the PGRDF employs a cost-sharing mechanism where the government and private developers jointly fund exploratory drilling. This risk-sharing approach aims to mitigate the high financial risks associated with early-stage geothermal projects.

Once a project is deemed commercially viable, the developer repays the government’s share of the exploration costs, allowing the PGRDF to fund additional projects. The PGRDF also facilitates financing for viable projects through a refinancing window, further reducing risks for developers and attracting investment. Additionally, the facility promotes knowledge sharing and industry best practices by requiring developers to share drilling data and adhere to international standards. By providing financial support, technical expertise, and a conducive regulatory environment, the PGRDF aims to unlock the full potential of the Philippines’ geothermal resources.

column4: Waste to Energy Project
column6:
The MMDA Metro Manila 25-year SWM Master Plan provides the overarching strategies on waste management for Metro Manila envisioning "Ecologically sound solid waste management towards clean and litter-free Metropolitan Manila". It recognizes the direct need to increase capacities for waste disposal and to process the waste generated to useful products like composts, refuse devired fuel and electric power via thermal and biological processes.

The Waste to Energy Project aligns with the sustainable development goals particularly, SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). It aims to:
     (1) reduce the volume of waste sent to the existing sanitary landfills thereby extending the lifespan of existing sites and reducing the need for converting lands into new landfill sites. 
     (2) contribute to reducing the dependence on fossil fuels through production of energy and enhancing energy security. 
     (3) Metro Manila to provide a model for sustainable waste management for other parts of the country using advanced available technology.

Thermal treatment extract energy from the waste while reducing its volume and rendering the remaining fraction mostly inert. The mechanical treatment (MT), that would sort waste at an MRF, together with an incineration facility shall compose the Waste to Energy Project. The total cost is estimated at Php 6 billion considering 3% inflation per annum to cover (a) construction of an incineration facility and a recycling sorting facility, (b) equipment, (c) site development, and (d) indirect cost.

The project provides non-incremental benefits considering health expenditures, tipping fees and incremental benefits such as reduction on the required land for disposal, extension of existing sanitary landfills, electricity sales from processed wastes, and employment multiplier. The power generated by the facility will benefit the host LGU in form of a share that maybe used to subsidize power supply to residents.

column4: VISAYAS RECORDS CENTER AND ARCHIVES
column6:
The National Archives of the Philippines-Regional Archival Network, Cebu, was established to provide extension services and functions related to managing public records and archives administration and control in the Visayas Regions (Region Vl, VII & VIII). It also operates public records and archives repositories for the Visayas regions and provides access.

As an extension office, the Regional Archival Network –Cebu's operational functions are divided into Records Center and Archives Services, which represent the functions of the main office's Archives and Records Center Divisions and are tasked with providing technical assistance and advice in Records Transfer, Processing and Arranging Records, Reference Service, and Maintenance and Security of Records. 

RAN-Cebu has a total record holding of 341.124002 cu. m. The Archives holds  163.07918 cu.m. while the Records Center has 178.044822 cu. m., and the only NAP satellite office hasn’t been granted a permanent building. Since its establishment in 1980, the agency has been leasing and hasn’t been able to acquire any property to house its holdings permanently and for an office. This year, the office recently transferred its new location to Clotilde Commercial Center, M.L. Quezon Avenue, Casuntingan, Mandaue City, which has a lot of 900 sq. m. Palawan Resources Corporation owns the building with a rent amounting to Php—443,520.00 per month. An additional 450 sq m. of the rented warehouse was also acquired as an extra storage facility with a monthly rental of Php 135,520.00. 

Finally, The said project is under the administration's eight-point (8) agenda: Create more Jobs, Create Quality Jobs, and Ensure a level playing field. It also falls within the Sustainable Development Goals: Gender Equality, Decent Work & Economic Growth, and Industry, Innovation & Infrastructure. 

The RAN-Cebu is willing to accept the transfer of permanent records and archival collections from different government agencies within the Visayas Region. However, the existing office can only accommodate limited records transfers. Thus, a permanent office building and additional storage facilities are needed for future transfers. 

This proposal was made in compliance with RA 9470 (Art. II, Sec.6 Par. C number 2), which stated, “Facilitate the acquisition of a permanent and suitable building for the National Archives to house the country’s archival holdings and public records. " By implementing this project, the office can better execute its mandate.

column4: Construction of  A Two-Storey Extension Building
column6:
In 2008, the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Regional Office No. 3 Building was designed and constructed to house various offices that provide frontline and technical services to the Commission’s stakeholders, with approximately thirty (30) personnel. 

In 2025, the number of staff and personnel has increased from thirty (30) to eighty-four (84) to respond to the pressing and growing demands of the clients. The increase in human resources has also been complemented by the rise in the number of information and communication (ICT) facilities, as well as furniture and fixtures. Moreover, over the course of three decades of regional operations, documents have accumulated, including Special Orders, Enrollment Lists,  program applications, school and student records, scholarship records, and liquidation reports. These changes are attributed to the Commission’s commitment to providing effective and efficient public services. However, there are limited upgrades in terms of operating capacity and space in the regional office. 

Based on the current situation, the first floor of the existing facility is occupied by the Administrative Division. On average, there are eight (8) employees occupying a 243 square feet room. Moreover, the second floor is being occupied by the Technical Division and some of the scholarship units, with a relative average of eighteen (18) occupants per 947 square feet size room.  In both rooms there is a set of ICT equipment, and furniture and fixtures per each staff member, including documents and other necessary things for work. Thus, there is limited space for each individual to move through the space to access various areas and interact with colleagues. Furthermore, due to its structural design, there are limited staff and documents occupying the third floor. With this inadequate space, the flow and circulation of people are affected which imposes threat to safety in times of disaster and emergency. 

To address these challenges, with the consideration of the limitation on structural alteration of the existing building, the proposed extension of the building will be necessary for the Commission to continue its provision of effective and efficient public services. The proposed extension will be used for Higher Education Management Information System Unit (HEMIS), which will strengthen its data access, management and analytics. column4: Design & Build of PN Command & Control Facility, Naval Station Jose Francisco, Fort Bonifacio Taguig
column6:
The Transfer of HPN Command and Control Facility is to be located at the Navy Village in Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City. The site is near BCDA`s newest development for government institutions (ex. Senate Building) and commercial establishments.

 The HPN Complex, which is envisioned to be green building-certified, will serve the Philippine Navy required functions and operations, and thus the following space allocations are anticipated: 2 level basements for parking, multi-functional ceremonial hall, conference rooms, executive rooms, and offices, workstations to various staff and offices, museum and libraries, public assistance office, cafeteria, Troops messing area, Media lounge, and general waiting area. Other duties of the complex include security, health, information technology, and communications, storage, and MEPF (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Fire Protection). 

The proposed transfer of the Headquarters Philippine Navy (HPN) Command and Control Facility will be implemented through the Design and Build (D&B) Concept, an approach that combines the design and construction phases under a single contract. This method ensures a streamlined process, allowing for faster project completion by eliminating the need for separate bidding processes. It also fosters close collaboration between the design and construction teams, ensuring that the plans are practical, efficient, and aligned with the Navy’s requirements. With a single entity accountable for the entire project, the D&B approach reduces the risks of delays, cost overruns, and mismatches between design and execution. This setup also promotes innovative solutions, as contractors are encouraged to propose creative and sustainable designs suited to the facility’s operational needs. By implementing this approach, the Philippine Navy can achieve a high-quality, strategically located Command and Control Facility that meets its current and future demands while optimizing resources and time.

Furthermore, the development strives to be green and sustainable, preferring ecologically responsible and energy-efficient materials and facilities throughout the construction process as well as building operations and maintenance.

The proposed project would transform the new Headquarters of PN with reliable and modern facilities and services that enable the headquarters to carry out responsive and effective support in carrying out its specific tasks within the structure of PN.

column4: Skyway 1 and 2 Improvement Projects
column6:
The proposed Skyway 1 & 2 Improvement Projects are composed of the following:

1)	Skyway Extension:

This component provides direct access between the southern areas of Luzon and Skyway, improving travel experience of motorists in the area, especially during peak hours.

•	Additional three (3) lanes and ramp along the northbound (to Manila) of Skyway from SLEX Muntinlupa to Skyway Main Toll Plaza.
•	Additional two (2) lanes and ramps are provided along the southbound (to Laguna) of the Skyway Main Toll Plaza to SLEX Muntinlupa.
•	Northbound ramp provided from Alabang (via Alabang-Zapote Road) to Skyway.

2)	Skyway Widening:

This component provides a long-term solution to alleviate the congestion being experienced by motorists along the Skyway section from Buendia to Muntinlupa. An additional one (1) lane shall be provided along the said section to increase the vehicle capacity for both north/south-bound traffic and improve the overall network performance of the expressway. 

3)	Skyway to NAIAX Bypass: Bypass ramp from Skyway directly to NAIAX.

This component intends to provide an approximately 1.0-kilometer, 7.0-meter-wide, two (2)-lane bypass ramp from Skyway southbound directly to NAIAX. This alleviates the weaving conflict being experienced along Skyway, particularly during peak hours, between vehicles going to NAIAX and traffic coming from the Magallanes on-ramp. This improvement enhances NAIAX – Skyway interconnectivity.

4)	EDSA On-Ramp to Skyway: Two (2)-lane on-ramp to Skyway from EDSA.

This component will provide a 420-meter, two (2)-lane, northbound Skyway access ramp from EDSA. Without this ramp, vehicles from EDSA will have to access the northbound Skyway Stage 3 via an on-ramp located farther north, in Buendia.

5)	New Decongestion Facilities:

The New Decongestion Facilities consists of two (2) new lines to improve the interconnectivity of Skyway to the highly urbanized areas of Bicutan and Sucat:

•	Skyway - Bicutan East

The 1.80-kilometer, Skyway-Bicutan East elevated segment connects with Skyway at Central Bicutan (near SLEX Bicutan Exit), traverses east along General Santos Avenue, and links C6 in Upper Bicutan. This will decongest the Bicutan Exit by providing direct connections to the Skyway, bypassing the busy SLEX at-grade section.

•	Sucat East – NAIAX

The 9.25-kilometer, Sucat East-NAIAX segment begins with a connection to the Bicutan Sucat East/Sucat-Alabang East proposed segments and with Skyway at Upper Sucat in Muntinlupa. The alignment then traverses westward along Parañaque-Sucat Road, travels north in San Dionisio, Parañaque towards Ninoy Aquino/Imelda Avenue, and finally links with NAIAX near NAIA Terminal 1. This link will enhance connectivity of NAIA with Skyway, SLEX and regions south of Metro Manila.

column4: Naval Reserve Command Mobilization Centers
column6:
The proposed project involves the construction of a Naval Reserve Mobilization Center at Camp Tiniguiban, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan. The facility is envisioned to provide a dedicated space capable of accommodating one (1) Naval Squadron or two (2) Marine Companies at any given time, thereby supporting the organization, training, and mobilization requirements of the Naval Reserve Force in Western Command’s (WESCOM) area of responsibility.
The Mobilization Center will serve as the primary venue for the conduct of the Basic Citizen Military Course (BCMC) and other naval reservist training programs designed to develop the skills, discipline, and readiness of reservists. It will also function as the designated reporting and assembly area for reservists during mobilization, ensuring order, efficiency, and accountability in the integration of reserve forces with active units. Furthermore, the facility will include provisions for the temporary storage of equipment and materiel in preparation for mobilization and deployment.
By establishing this dedicated center, the project will address the current lack of suitable infrastructure to house, train, and organize naval reservists in Palawan, a province of strategic maritime importance. It will enhance the capability of the Naval Reserve Command to support national defense objectives, respond to contingencies, and conduct humanitarian assistance and disaster response (HADR) operations. In the long term, the Naval Reserve Mobilization Center will serve as a force multiplier, strengthening the readiness, reliability, and integration of the naval reservists into the total force concept of the Philippine Navy and Armed Forces of the Philippines.

column4: Rehabilitation and Protection of Water Resources Supporting Irrigation System (R&P WRSIS)
column6:
To improve the present bio-physical condition of the  watershed supporting irrigation system and reduce the rapid denudation of the forest  cover and erosion caused by natural and human activities within and near the catchment area. The improvement of degraded irrigation water resources will increase food production by making the irrigation system sustainable and viable.

Degradation of irrigation water sources is the major problem contributing to the accelerated soil erosion that result in sedimentation confronting the sustainable operation of irrigation systems in the country. This problem entails an increase in  operation costs and maintenance of irrigation facilities requiring frequent rehabilitation.  Therefore, rehabilitation and protection of water resources supporting the  24  National  irrigation systems  and 8,400 Communal Irrigation System  of Region 02 was proposed to maintain efficiency and serviceability of irrigation  systems and reduce operation and maintenance cost.

To address issues and concerns of accelerated  soil erosion and sediment deposition to the irrigation facilities resulting in inefficient  delivery of irrigation water supply in the service area. It is anticipated that after the program has been implemented, the Agency will improve performance of the irrigation  system including equitable water distribution in timely and water deliveries of irrigation water supply in the service area. As a result, the improvement of performance of the irrigation system may yield to higher irrigation cropping intensity and create a higher  opportunity of farmers for better agricultural production. In addition, the reduction of cost for frequent desilting may translate to a better economic and financial viability of  NIA.

column4: Mines and Geosciences Bureau Regional Office No. XII Laboratory Building Construction
column6:
Sampling preparation is the first step of every process of physical and chemical analysis. But as of this moment, the Mines and Geosciences Bureau-XIl's samples are either sent to the MGBCO or sourced out to other third-party.

The construction of a new laboratory building is necessary for the operationalization of the General Laboratory Services Section which provides laboratory services in Region 12. This will also allow MGB-XII to perform one of its functions based on the revised organizational structure and functions of the Mines and Geosciences Bureau under DAO 2015-06 ("Providing for the Revised Organizational Structure and Function of the Mines and Geosciences Bureau Pursuant to its Approved Rationalization Plan"), Section 2.2.2.4 created a laboratory section that would provide services on the geological laboratory analysis of minerals/ores, rocks, soil, sediments, fossils, water. and other types of samples.

Although MGB-XII has an existing laboratory building, currently it is utilized as the MGB-XII office. Since the building has already been retrofitted as an office building, the current allotted area for the laboratory unit has become limited and does not conform to the ideal standard area for an operational laboratory.

MGB-XII also aims to mitigate health hazards in accordance to the QESHMS Policy to provide a safe and healthy working environment for its employees by separating the laboratory unit as it poses health threats if ever the laboratory becomes functional in the MGB-XII Building.

column4: Philippine Conventional Energy Contracting Program (PCECP)
column6:
The PCECP, implemented through the Locally Funded Project “Strategic Promotion of Petroleum Exploration through the PCECP”, is a significant licensing scheme implemented by the Philippine government to enhance petroleum exploration in the country. The primary objective of the PCECP is to attract both local and international upstream petroleum players, allowing for increased participation and investment in the Philippine energy sector. By offering flexible modes of licensing, the program aims to generate new technical data that can contribute to the country's energy independence and resiliency.

The PCECP Project, being able to provide for the necessary resources, allows implementors to equip themselves, its support units/personnel and the Department to effectively engage with its stakeholders in continuously promoting petroleum exploration in the country. To that end, the project provides avenues for DOE to reach out to diverse range of companies, including both established operators and new entrants that may share their expertise and introduce innovative approaches, thus expanding our knowledge base to ultimately spur growth and development in the Philippine upstream petroleum industry.

Petroleum exploration being a data-intensive endeavor, the government aims to generate new technical data through the award of new Petroleum Service Contracts (PSCs). Petroleum exploration involves conducting geological surveys, seismic studies, and drilling wells to identify potential oil, gas, and native hydrogen reserves. By allowing more companies to engage in exploration activities, the program can generate a wealth of new data that can enhance the understanding of the country's petroleum potential. This data can be used to attract further investment, as it provides valuable insights into the feasibility and commercial viability of future oil, gas, and native hydrogen projects.

The PCECP also plays a crucial role in the Philippines' pursuit of energy independence and resiliency. As an archipelagic nation, the Philippines heavily relies on imported energy sources to meet its growing demand. By promoting petroleum exploration and development, the country aims to reduce its dependence on foreign energy supplies and achieve greater energy self-sufficiency. This can lead to improved energy security, reduced import costs, and increased revenue from domestic petroleum resources.

Further, the PCECP aligns with the government's broader energy policies and strategies. It supports the Philippines' commitment to diversifying its energy mix and ensuring energy security as the country journeys toward the energy transition, while still being cognizant of the important role of developing and utilizing our indigenous petroleum resources in achieving such goals. Likewise, the program contributes to the government's efforts to attract sustainable investments in the energy sector, fostering economic growth, job creation, and technological advancements

To ensure the success of the PCECP, the government would establish clear guidelines, regulations, and contractual terms that govern the licensing process and the obligations of contractors. These measures aim to provide a transparent and stable investment environment, protecting the interests of both the government and the participating companies. The program would likely incorporate environmental safeguards and regulations to ensure responsible and sustainable exploration practices.

column4: NATIONAL ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVATION PROGRAM
column6:
The NATIONAL ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVATION PROGRAM (NEECP) is a government initiative aimed at rationalizing the nation's demand for petroleum products and electricity, with the goal of mitigating the economic impact of rising energy prices. Initially launched on August 28, 2004, by former President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo, the program seeks to cultivate a culture of "EC Way of Life" among t he populace, emphasizing energy efficiency and conservation as integral components of daily living. It serves as a foundational framework for government efforts to promote the efficient and responsible use of energy resources.

At its core, the NEECP aims to integrate energy efficiency and conservation practices into both individual and business routines. By implementing strategies to optimize energy consumption, the program aims to offset the effects of escalating petroleum and electricity costs. It strives to achieve savings in fuel and electricity expenses while maintaining productivity levels and encourages participation from diverse sectors to contribute to overall energy conservation efforts. Additionally, the program underscores the significance of environmental stewardship by curbing energy-related emissions and endorsing sustainable practices.

Through these concerted endeavors, the NEECP endeavors to embed energy efficiency and conservation as intrinsic aspects of the Filipino lifestyle. By fostering conscientious energy usage, the program aims to bolster economic resilience, diminish dependence on expensive energy sources, and uphold environmental sustainability principles.

column4: Nuclear Energy Program Implementing Organizations (NEPIO)
column6:
The NEPIO in the Philippines is responsible for coordinating the efforts and activities of various organizations involved in nuclear infrastructure development. The NEPIO is led by a Steering Committee headed by an Undersecretary, supported by other senior officials from the DOE.

To ensure effective and timely implementation of its functions and responsibilities, the DOE has established technical working groups (TWGs) within its bureaus and services. These TWGs are assigned to address the 19 infrastructure issues outlined in each milestone of a nuclear power program.

These infrastructure issues encompass a wide range of aspects related to the development of a nuclear energy program. Some of the key issues include Nuclear Safety, Management Funding and Financing, Legislative Framework, Safeguards, Regulatory Framework, Radiation Protection, Electrical Grid, Human Resources Development, Stakeholder Involvement, Site and Supporting Facilities, Environmental Protection, Emergency Planning, Security and Physical Protection, Nuclear Fuel Cycle, Radioactive Waste, Industrial Involvement, and Procurement.

Each issue requires careful consideration and planning to ensure the successful establishment and operation of a nuclear power program. The TWGs within the DOE bureaus and services are responsible for addressing these issues and working towards the development of a comprehensive and robust nuclear infrastructure.
By coordinating the efforts of these organizations and addressing the 19 infrastructure issues, the NEPIO aims to lay the foundation for the implementation of a safe, secure, and sustainable nuclear energy program in the Philippines.

Per Department Order 2024-01-0001, the DOE Nuclear Energy Program Coordinating Committee (NEP-CC) is created to ensure the effective participation of the DOE in the Nuclear Energy Program Inter-Agency Committee (NEP-IAC) pursuant to Executive Order (EO) 164, series of 2022. column4: Oil Industry Deregulation Management Program
column6:
The Oil Industry Deregulation Management Program (OIDMP) in the Philippines was established in line with Republic Act 8479, also known as the Downstream Oil Industry Deregulation Act of 1998. The main objective of this law is to ensure a competitive market with fair prices and a continuous supply of environmentally clean and high-quality petroleum products. The deregulation of the downstream oil industry encouraged competition and the entry of new players into the market.

To effectively implement the objectives of the law, the OIDMP allocated funds to support various programs, projects, and activities. These initiatives are designed to help the OIMB implement its functions, including policy formulation, development, and monitoring of quality, safety, and environmental standards.

The OIDMP focuses on promoting fair trade practices and ensuring consumer protection. It aims to create a level playing field for all market participants and safeguard the interests of consumers. This involves monitoring compliance with quality and safety standards, as well as implementing measures to prevent anti-competitive practices.

By allocating resources to the OIDMP, the Philippine government aims to ensure the effective implementation of deregulation measures in the oil industry. The program supports the objectives of Republic Act 8479 by facilitating competition, encouraging the provision of high-quality petroleum products, and protecting consumer rights.

column4: Samar - Leyte Railway
column6:
The Samar-Leyte Railway (SLR) Project is a strategic initiative under the Philippine Railway System designed to address the absence of rail transport in Eastern Visayas (Region VIII). At present, the movement of people and goods in the region relies heavily on road-based transport, resulting in high logistics costs, limited connectivity, and constraints on economic growth and accessibility.

The proposed railway project seeks to transform regional mobility and development by:
- Improving mobility across Samar and Leyte through efficient rail services.
- Connecting rural and urban areas more effectively to enhance accessibility.
- Facilitating the movement of goods to reduce transport costs and improve supply chain efficiency.
- Supporting inclusive regional development by linking communities to growth centers and opportunities.

Aligned with national and regional planning frameworks, the project supports the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, which emphasizes resilient and sustainable infrastructure, and the Visayas Spatial Development Framework (VSDF) 2015–2045, which prioritizes improved connectivity and reduced geographic disparities.

The Department of Transportation (DOTr), in partnership with the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) and the Regional Development Council (RDC) VIII, will serve as the Implementing and Executing Agency for the Samar-Leyte Railway Project, ensuring coordinated planning, execution, and delivery of outcomes that advance regional integration and long-term economic growth.

column4: Strengthening Governance
column6:
The Strengthening Governance Program of Pangasinan State University aims to improve institutional efficiency, safety, and operational resilience through the development and upgrading of core campus infrastructure. The program covers the construction and rehabilitation of essential governance related facilities such as internal access roads, campus road networks, drainage and flood mitigation systems, one stop shop administration buildings, shared service facilities, water impounding systems, and materials recovery facilities. These projects are designed to enhance campus mobility, ensure environmental safety, streamline administrative processes, and support effective service delivery across all PSU campuses.

The program includes the development of climate resilient and disaster responsive infrastructure that addresses recurring issues such as flooding, waste management, and limited access routes. The construction of road networks and internal access roads aims to improve campus circulation, emergency response, and logistical efficiency. The establishment of drainage systems, water impounding structures, and MRFs supports environmental sustainability, disaster preparedness, and compliance with national environmental regulations. Governance support facilities such as administration buildings and shared service centers are intended to centralize operations, improve transaction efficiency, and strengthen institutional management systems.

Overall, the Strengthening Governance Program seeks to create a safe, efficient, and well managed campus environment that enhances institutional performance and supports PSU’s academic, research, and extension functions. By aligning infrastructure development with the Regional Development Investment Program (RDIP) and national priorities on good governance, disaster resilience, and sustainable development, the program contributes to long term institutional stability and improved public service delivery.

column4: Smart Campus Modernization Program for Philippine Science High School - Ilocos Region Campus in Ilocos Sur
column6:
The Smart Campus Modernization Program responds to critical developmental and capacity gaps at the Philippine Science High School – Ilocos Region Campus resulting from the expansion of student intake under the Philippine Science High School System. In recent years, PSHSS has increased student intake in many of its regional campuses from three (3) sections to four (4) sections per grade level. However, several campuses, including PSHS–Ilocos Region Campus in Ilocos Sur, were originally designed to accommodate only ninety (90) students per grade level, based on three sections with thirty (30) students each. The increase to one hundred twenty (120) students per grade level has placed significant pressure on existing academic and support facilities, necessitating additional learning spaces to maintain optimal class sizes, laboratory standards, and the quality of science education.
Compounding this issue, several academic and support facilities are aging, undersized, or no longer fully compliant with current safety, accessibility, and disaster resilience standards. Existing classrooms, laboratories, dormitories, utilities, and common facilities have limited capacity to support the increased student population and are not fully configured for advanced digital learning, research activities, and smart campus systems.
To address these gaps, the program will undertake the construction, upgrading, rehabilitation, and expansion of academic buildings, laboratories, learning spaces, dormitories, and support facilities to accommodate increased enrollment while preserving PSHS’ standards for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. Infrastructure upgrades will include improvements to structural integrity, power, water, data, and network backbone systems to ensure readiness for smart technology integration.

Through this initiative, PSHS–Ilocos Region Campus will be better equipped to support increased student enrollment while continuing to deliver high-quality, future-ready science education for the Ilocos Region.

column4: Smart Campus Modernization Program for Philippine Science High School - Main Campus in Diliman Quezon City
column6:
The Smart Campus Modernization Program responds to critical developmental, safety, and capacity gaps at the Philippine Science High School – Main Campus, the flagship campus of the Philippine Science High School System (PSHSS). Established more than six (6) decades ago, the campus houses aging academic and support facilities that require immediate retrofitting and modernization to ensure continued compliance with current safety, accessibility, and disaster resilience standards, while meeting the evolving demands of a growing student population and a technology-driven learning environment.

In line with the system-wide expansion of student intake under the K to 12 Program, PSHS MC has expanded enrollment to include two additional grade levels and continues to serve as the primary benchmark for academic excellence, research capability, and smart campus implementation across the System. However, many of its buildings and core infrastructure were originally designed to accommodate a significantly smaller population and earlier pedagogical models, and have not been comprehensively upgraded to support contemporary STEM instruction, advanced research activities, and digital learning systems expected of the flagship campus.

At present, there remains a need for fifteen (15) additional laboratories to adequately support advanced science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) instruction, research, and innovation activities. Moreover, PSHS MC faces a deficit of twelve (12) dormitory rooms, constraining its capacity to provide safe and adequate residential accommodation for students, particularly those coming from distant provinces.

Compounding these gaps, a significant portion of campus facilities—many of which are over 60 years old—are structurally aging, undersized, or no longer fully compliant with prevailing standards on structural safety, fire protection, accessibility, and disaster risk reduction, including seismic resilience. Utilities and support systems such as power, water, sanitation, drainage, and ICT backbone infrastructure are likewise outdated and have limited capacity to support increased enrollment and integrated smart campus technologies.

To address these challenges, the program will undertake the retrofitting, rehabilitation, upgrading, and expansion of academic buildings, laboratories, learning spaces, dormitories, and essential support facilities. These interventions will prioritize structural strengthening, life-safety improvements, and climate- and disaster-resilient design, alongside upgrades to power, water, data, and network backbone systems to ensure full readiness for smart technology integration and system-wide interoperability.

Through this initiative, PSHS Main Campus will be strengthened as a safe, resilient, and future-ready flagship campus, capable of sustaining increased enrollment, serving as the model for smart campus development across the PSHSS, and delivering high-quality, inclusive, and globally competitive STEM education for learners nationwide

column4: Local Roads and Bridges Inventory Program (LRBIP)
column5: Department of the Interior and Local Government
column6:
Local road networks are vital to the Philippine economy, accounting for about 167,000 kilometers—or 83% of the country’s total road network—under the jurisdiction of local government units (LGUs). In contrast, national roads span approximately 35,500 kilometers (17%) and are managed by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH). To ensure comprehensive infrastructure data, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) serves as the sole agency responsible for consolidating the nationwide inventory of local roads and bridges.

A comprehensive and accurate inventory is essential for effective infrastructure management. Historically, the absence of a centralized system has led to fragmented planning, inefficient budgeting, and missed development opportunities. To address this, the DILG’s Office of Project Development Services (OPDS) developed the Road and Bridge Information System (RBIS)—a digital platform that consolidates and manages local road and bridge data nationwide.

column4: 4C Air Traffic Control Tower
column5: Aurora Pacific Economic Zone and Freeport Authority
column6:
The "4C Air Control Tower" likely refers to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Order 6480.4C, which outlines policies for siting new Airport Traffic Control Towers (ATCTs), ensuring safety in the National Airspace System by defining criteria for location, design, and approval. Essentially, it's a regulatory document guiding where and how tall towers are built to provide controllers optimal visibility for managing all aircraft movements (ground, takeoff, landing) and ensuring safe separation, using visual observation and technology to coordinate the busy airport environment. 
Key Aspects of FAA Order 6480.4C & Control Towers:
Siting Criteria: The order sets standards for where towers should be placed to give controllers the best view of runways, taxiways, and surrounding airspace.
Height & Visibility: Towers are tall, glass-enclosed structures designed for 360-degree visual contact with the entire airport surface and nearby air traffic.
Traffic Management: Controllers manage aircraft on the ground (Ground Control) and in the air near the airport (Tower/Local Control), issuing clearances for takeoffs and landings.
Technology Integration: Towers use radar, flight data, and communication systems, with Order 6480.4C ensuring new towers can support these advanced tools.
Safety & Efficiency: The ultimate goal is preventing collisions and ensuring smooth, orderly air traffic flow, as detailed in the FAA's ATC handbook. 
In short, Order 6480.4C is the rulebook for building the essential tall structure (the ATCT) that acts as the airport's "nerve center" for safety and operations, ensuring optimal positioning and functionality for the air traffic controllers inside.

column4: BSWM - Drip Irrigation with Fertigation for Rice-Based Farm Diversification
column6:
Drip Irrigation System provides a slow and steady supply of water and fertilizer directly to the plant base, reducing water wastage and promoting efficient plant growth. 

The project aims to establish solar-powered irrigation system (SPIS) with drip irrigation to provide rice-based farmers with option for diversification of high value crops. 

This type of irrigation system can be employed in areas where water is scarce or limited. Rice-based farms can adopt drip irrigation systems for diversification to high-value crops especially when water is not enough for rice production.

Since drip irrigation requires power for pumping water to the pipe network, a typical SPIS can be matched with this type of irrigation system where solar power can be used as source of energy for both the main pump and pump for the drip irrigation system.

The project will irrigate 224 hectares of rice and 4.16 hectares of high-value crops across the country.

The Satellite-Based Platform for Integrated Infrastructure Planning, Monitoring, and Evaluation is a proposed DEPDev initiative that aims to strengthen infrastructure governance by integrating satellite imagery, geospatial data, project information, and socioeconomic indicators into a centralized decision-support system.

The platform addresses long-standing challenges such as fragmented agency databases, limited interoperability, and reliance on self-reported administrative data by enabling near-real-time, independently verifiable monitoring of infrastructure projects across their full lifecycle—from planning and prioritization to implementation and evaluation.

By linking spatial intelligence with financial and performance data, and incorporating hazard, environmental, and climate-risk datasets, the platform supports evidence-based planning, transparency, and accountability, while enhancing cross-agency coordination and resilience-oriented infrastructure decision-making in line with Executive Order No. 72 (s. 2024) and Republic Act No. 12145.
